1.overview: The descendants of Jacob, who entered Egypt as seventy people, multiply after Joseph and his generation die, and a new king enslaves them out of fear of their numbers. Pharaoh orders the Hebrew midwives Shiphrah and Puah to kill newborn boys, but they let them live, and Pharaoh then commands all Egyptians to throw Hebrew sons into the Nile.

2.overview: Moses is born to a Levite woman, rescued from the Nile by Pharaoh’s daughter, and raised as her son. After killing an Egyptian, he flees to Midian, marries Zipporah, and becomes a father, while Israel’s cries reach God, who remembers his covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

3.overview: At Horeb, the LORD appears to Moses in a burning bush, identifies himself as the God of the patriarchs, and commissions Moses to lead Israel out of Egypt. God reveals the name I AM, directs Moses to approach Israel’s elders and Pharaoh, and promises deliverance, a journey to Canaan, and Egyptian goods.

sections.heading: God’s Name and Instructions to Moses

4.overview: The LORD gives Moses signs to answer Israel’s doubts, promises help with his speech, appoints Aaron as his spokesman, and warns that Pharaoh’s refusal to release Israel will bring the death of his firstborn. Moses returns toward Egypt with his family, Zipporah circumcises their son at a lodging place, and Aaron joins Moses to present the LORD’s words and signs to Israel’s elders, who believe and worship.

5.overview: Moses and Aaron ask Pharaoh to let Israel go into the wilderness to worship the LORD, but Pharaoh refuses and increases the Israelites’ brickmaking burden by withholding straw. The Israelite foremen appeal to Pharaoh, then blame Moses and Aaron for their worsening plight, and Moses asks the LORD why he has sent him when Israel remains oppressed.

sections.heading: Straw Withheld and Brick Quotas Enforced
Foremen Appeal to Pharaoh and Confront Moses

6.overview: The LORD promises to free Israel from Egyptian bondage, make the Israelites his people, and bring them into the land promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; they do not listen to Moses, and Moses questions whether Pharaoh will hear him. The LORD charges Moses and Aaron to bring Israel out, and a genealogy traces the families of Reuben, Simeon, and Levi, identifying Aaron and Moses before the LORD repeats his command to Moses.

sections.heading: The families of Israel and Levi

7.overview: The LORD commissions Moses and Aaron to confront Pharaoh, predicts Pharaoh’s resistance, and says Egypt will know that he is the LORD when he brings Israel out. Aaron’s staff becomes a serpent before Pharaoh, and Aaron then strikes the Nile, turning Egypt’s waters to blood; Pharaoh remains unmoved as the Egyptians seek drinking water and seven days pass.

8.overview: The LORD sends frogs, gnats, and swarms of flies over Egypt through Moses and Aaron, while Pharaoh repeatedly hardens his heart and refuses to release Israel. Pharaoh asks for relief and offers limited permission to sacrifice, but the LORD distinguishes Goshen from Egypt during the fly plague and Pharaoh again breaks his promise.

sections.heading: The Plague of Flies and Pharaoh’s Refusal

9.overview: The LORD sends a livestock plague and boils on Egypt, while distinguishing Israel from Egypt, but Pharaoh refuses to release the Israelites. The LORD sends devastating hail after warning Pharaoh’s officials; Pharaoh admits his wrongdoing and promises release, but hardens his heart again when the storm ends.

10.overview: Moses and Aaron warn Pharaoh of a locust plague, while Pharaoh’s officials urge him to release Israel and Pharaoh offers to let only the men go. The locusts devastate Egypt and are removed after Pharaoh seeks relief, but he again refuses release; darkness then covers Egypt, and Pharaoh orders Moses away after demanding Israel leave its livestock behind.

sections.heading: Warning of Locusts and Pharaoh’s Offer

11.overview: The LORD tells Moses that one final plague will lead Pharaoh to drive Israel out, and instructs the people to ask the Egyptians for silver and gold as Moses gains their favor. Moses announces the death of Egypt’s firstborn and the distinction between Egypt and Israel, while the LORD says Pharaoh will not listen and hardens his heart against releasing Israel.

sections.heading: The Final Plague and Egyptian Favor

12.overview: The LORD gives Moses and Aaron instructions for the Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread, and Moses relays them to Israel. After the LORD strikes Egypt’s firstborn, Pharaoh sends Israel away; the people depart with possessions and a mixed multitude, and the chapter sets out further Passover regulations as the LORD brings Israel out of Egypt.

sections.heading: The Firstborn Struck and Israel Departs

13.overview: The LORD commands the consecration of Israel’s firstborn, and Moses instructs the people to keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread and redeem their firstborn sons as memorials of the exodus from Egypt. God leads Israel away from the Philistine road toward the Red Sea, Moses carries Joseph’s bones, and pillars of cloud and fire guide the people.

sections.heading: Israel’s Route and the Guiding Pillars

14.overview: The LORD directs Israel to camp by the sea, hardens Pharaoh’s heart, and sends the Egyptian army in pursuit; Moses tells the terrified Israelites that the LORD will fight for them. The LORD parts the sea so Israel crosses on dry ground, then returns the waters over Pharaoh’s army, and Israel sees the LORD’s power and believes in Him and Moses.

15.overview: Moses and the Israelites sing of the LORD’s victory over Pharaoh’s army, and Miriam leads the women in a song celebrating the same deliverance. At Marah the LORD sweetens bitter water and gives Israel a statute and test, and the people then camp at Elim, where water and palm trees are plentiful.

sections.heading: Moses’ Song of the LORD’s Victory

16.overview: Israel grumbles in the Desert of Sin over food, and the LORD promises quail and daily bread, with a double portion on the sixth day. Quail and manna arrive, the people receive instructions for gathering and Sabbath rest, and an omer of manna is preserved as the food sustains Israel until the border of Canaan.

sections.heading: Israel Grumbles and the LORD Promises Food
Quail and Manna in the Camp
The Sixth-Day Provision and Sabbath Rest

17.overview: At Rephidim, Israel quarrels with Moses over the lack of water, and the LORD provides water from a rock at Horeb; Moses names the place Massah and Meribah. When Amalek attacks, Joshua leads Israel’s fight as Aaron and Hur support Moses, and the LORD commands a written reminder before Moses builds an altar and declares the LORD’s continuing war against Amalek.

sections.heading: Water from the Rock at Horeb

18.overview: Jethro visits Moses in the wilderness with Zipporah and their sons, hears how the LORD delivered Israel from Egypt, and praises the LORD. Seeing Moses judge the people alone, Jethro advises him to appoint capable leaders to handle routine cases, and Moses adopts the arrangement before Jethro returns home.

sections.heading: Jethro Visits and Praises the LORD

19.overview: Israel arrives at Mount Sinai, where the LORD offers the people a covenant calling them his treasured possession, a kingdom of priests, and a holy nation, and they agree to obey. The LORD prepares to descend before the people amid thunder, fire, and a trembling mountain, while Moses receives repeated warnings to keep them from approaching the mountain.

sections.heading: Israel Arrives at Sinai and Accepts the Covenant
The LORD Descends and Sets Boundaries

20.overview: The LORD identifies himself as Israel’s deliverer from Egypt and gives commandments concerning worship, the Sabbath, family, and conduct toward others. The Israelites fear the signs at Mount Sinai and ask Moses to speak for them, after which the LORD gives instructions for altars and offerings.

21.overview: The ordinances address the release and treatment of Hebrew servants, penalties for violence and injury, and restitution for harm caused by animals or uncovered pits. They distinguish between intentional and accidental harm and set compensation or penalties for cases involving death, bodily injury, and property loss.

sections.heading: Restitution for Animal and Property Damage

22.overview: The chapter sets out restitution and liability rules for theft, property damage, safekeeping, borrowed animals, and seduction, then prescribes penalties for sorcery, bestiality, and sacrifice to other gods. It gives commands concerning foreigners, widows, orphans, poor borrowers, pledges, offerings, firstborn, and the conduct expected of Israel as the LORD’s holy people.

23.overview: The chapter sets out laws on truthful testimony, impartial justice, care for others, the land’s rest, the Sabbath, and the annual feasts. The LORD promises an angel’s guidance, protection, and blessing as Israel enters the land, while warning against its gods and covenants with its inhabitants.

sections.heading: The angel and the LORD’s promises
Conquest and boundaries of the land

24.overview: Moses presents the LORD’s words to Israel, records the covenant, and seals it with offerings and blood after the people pledge obedience. Moses, Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and Israel’s elders see God, and Moses then ascends Mount Sinai to receive the stone tablets and remains there forty days and nights.

25.overview: The LORD tells Moses to collect offerings from the Israelites and directs them to build a sanctuary according to the pattern shown on the mountain. He specifies the ark and mercy seat, the table for the Bread of the Presence, and the gold lampstand and its utensils.

sections.heading: The Table and Bread of the Presence

26.overview: The instructions specify the tabernacle’s linen and goat-hair curtains, outer coverings, acacia frames, silver bases, and gold crossbars. They describe the inner veil separating the Holy Place from the Most Holy Place, the placement of the ark, mercy seat, table, and lampstand, and the entrance curtain and its posts.

27.overview: The chapter gives instructions for a bronze altar, including its utensils, grate, and carrying poles, and sets out the dimensions and materials of the tabernacle courtyard. It also directs the Israelites to provide pure olive oil and assigns Aaron and his sons to tend the lamps in the Tent of Meeting from evening until morning.

28.overview: The LORD directs Moses to appoint Aaron and his sons as priests and to have skilled craftsmen make their holy garments. The instructions describe the ephod and breastpiece bearing Israel’s tribal names, the robe and headpiece marked “HOLY TO THE LORD,” and garments for Aaron’s sons, along with requirements for consecration and service.

sections.heading: Aaron and His Sons as Priests

29.overview: The LORD instructs Moses to consecrate Aaron and his sons as priests through washing, vesting, anointing, and a seven-day sequence of sacrifices and offerings. He establishes daily offerings at the Tent of Meeting and promises to meet Israel there, consecrate the sanctuary and priests, and dwell among the people as their God.

30.overview: The LORD instructs Moses to make the incense altar and establish its daily use and annual atonement, require a half-shekel ransom from counted Israelites, and provide a bronze basin for priestly washing. He gives the formula and restrictions for the sacred anointing oil and incense, and directs that the Tabernacle furnishings and Aaron and his sons be consecrated.

31.overview: The LORD appoints Bezalel and Oholiab and equips them and the other craftsmen to make the sanctuary, its furnishings, priestly garments, anointing oil, and incense. He commands Israel to keep the Sabbath as a permanent covenant sign, then gives Moses the stone tablets of the Testimony on Mount Sinai.

sections.heading: The Sabbath as a Covenant Sign

32.overview: While Moses is on the mountain, the Israelites make and worship a golden calf, and the LORD tells Moses that the people have corrupted themselves. Moses intercedes for them, breaks the tablets when he reaches the camp, directs the Levites to kill about three thousand people, and later pleads for forgiveness as the LORD promises judgment and sends a plague.

33.overview: The LORD tells Moses to lead Israel toward the promised land, but says his presence will not go with the stiff-necked people; Israel mourns, and Moses meets the LORD at the Tent of Meeting outside the camp. Moses asks for the LORD’s presence and glory, and the LORD promises to go with him, proclaim his name and goodness, and shield Moses in a cleft of rock so he sees only the LORD’s back.

sections.heading: Moses Asks to See the LORD’s Glory

34.overview: The LORD tells Moses to prepare new stone tablets, reveals his compassionate and just character on Mount Sinai, and renews the covenant with Israel through commands and festivals. After Moses spends forty days with the LORD and receives the covenant words, he descends with a radiant face and veils it when he is not speaking with the LORD.

sections.heading: New Tablets and the LORD’s Character

35.overview: Moses instructs Israel to observe the Sabbath and bring willing offerings and skilled labor for the tabernacle, its furnishings, and priestly garments. The Israelites contribute materials, and Moses identifies Bezalel and Oholiab, whom the LORD equips with skill and ability to teach others.

36.overview: Moses commissions Bezalel, Oholiab, and the skilled workers, who receive more offerings than the sanctuary work requires, so Moses stops further contributions. The workers make the tabernacle curtains and coverings, its acacia frames and crossbars, the inner veil, and the entrance curtain with their supports.

37.overview: Bezalel constructs the ark and mercy seat, the gold-covered table and its utensils, and the hammered-gold lampstand with its lamps. He makes the gold-covered altar of incense and its carrying poles, along with the sacred anointing oil and fragrant incense.

38.overview: Bezalel makes the bronze altar and basin, then constructs the courtyard and its embroidered entrance. The chapter records the tabernacle inventory under Ithamar’s direction, names Bezalel and Oholiab as craftsmen, and accounts for the gold, silver, and bronze used in the work.

39.overview: Bezalel and the Israelites make Aaron’s ephod, breastpiece, robe, and other priestly garments with the materials and details commanded by the LORD. They complete the tabernacle work, bring its furnishings and garments to Moses, and he inspects the work and blesses them.

40.overview: The LORD instructs Moses to set up and consecrate the tabernacle, its furnishings, and Aaron and his sons for priestly service, and Moses carries out the commands. The cloud covers the Tent of Meeting and the LORD’s glory fills the tabernacle, while the cloud and fire guide Israel’s journeys.

sections.heading: Instructions for the Tabernacle and Priests
The LORD’s Glory and Israel’s Guidance
